tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

## Scoping Rules for Squad A

- Do not modify `order-summary/` without notifying Squad B — it is Tier 2.
- Do not modify `use-current-basket.ts` — Tier 1, Integration lead owns it.
- Always scope to the specific partial — do not refactor the parent checkout page unless explicitly asked.
- Changes to express payment components require Integration lead awareness.
- `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — notify Squad B before any change.

**Fixing a spacing issue in the shipping address form:**
✅ `In overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/shipping-address.tsx only, adjust the Stack spacing prop from 6 to 3 at the base breakpoint. Do not modify any theme files, hooks, or other partials.`

9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path

13	 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
14	 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
15	 *
16	 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
17	 * component from a new component":
18	 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
19	 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
20	 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
21	 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
22	 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
23	 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
24	 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
25	 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
26	 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
27	 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
28	 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
29	 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
30	 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
31	 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
32	 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
33	 *
34	 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
35	 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
36	 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
39	 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
40	 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
43	 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
44	 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
45	 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
46	 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
47	 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
48	 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
49	 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
50	 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
51	 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
52	 * tested requirement.
53	 *
54	 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
55	 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
56	 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
57	 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
58	 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
59	 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
60	 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
61	 *
62	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
63	 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
65	 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
66	 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
67	 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
68	 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
69	 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
70	 *
71	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
72	 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
73	 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
74	 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
75	 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
76	 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
77	 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
78	 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
79	 *
80	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): `discountLabel` (optional, prop-driven) renders directly beneath the
81	 * stepper/price row: DOM order is stepper -> discountLabel -> message -> secondaryActions.
82	 * "Beneath the stepper" is sourced (session-notes.md line 394's own ticket-summary prose, and the
83	 * plan's own step 3.3 pass criterion 2 wording); placing it AHEAD of `message` specifically is
84	 * this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement — no citation
85	 * in session-notes.md sequences discountLabel relative to message (checked directly, not assumed),
86	 * and the pass criterion itself is satisfied by "beneath the stepper" alone regardless of order.
87	 * Chosen because a discount is a property of the line item's own state (always true or false for
88	 * that line), while `message` is closer to point-of-action feedback nearer the actions row — a
89	 * reasonable read, not a tested one. Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order.
90	 * Purely presentational, per session-notes.md §4's SFCC-795 decisions
91	 * ("Only the discount label is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired
92	 * when the promotions engine lands"): this component does not compute a discount percentage or
93	 * label itself; a caller supplies the already-resolved string once something upstream (the
94	 * promotions engine, and whatever cart-item mapper eventually feeds this component real basket
95	 * data) is wired — neither is built yet as of this commit. Undefined (every existing caller today)
96	 * renders nothing — no empty node is emitted. See the prop's own JSDoc below for the styling —
97	 * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node): a real Figma
98	 * citation exists now (this paragraph used to say none did, true only in the sense that none had
99	 * been pulled yet), and the label renders via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"` rather than
100	 * the bespoke, wrongly-precedented `<Text>` this component used to render directly.
101	 *
102	 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
103	 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
104	 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).
105	 * See this component's own test file for a disclosed, verified limitation on exactly where that
106	 * mechanism is and isn't reachable today.
107	 *
108	 * SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5, inserted 2026-09-18): the quantity-stepper branch below (the
109	 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)
110	 * now renders `ZimmQuantityStepper` (built and tested at step 3.1) instead of base-styled
111	 * `ProductQuantityPicker`, with `max` sourced from `getMaxOrderQuantity` (built and tested at
112	 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
113	 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
114	 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
115	 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
116	 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
117	 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
118	 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
119	 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to
120	 * local state via `setQuantity` if that call resolves truthy. Writing straight to `setQuantity`
121	 * instead (skipping the real mutation) would make the stepper look like it works while the real
122	 * basket on the server silently stops updating. `product-quantity-picker.tsx` itself is untouched
123	 * and, as of this commit, no longer imported anywhere in this file — left in place per this
124	 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new
125	 * stepper — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already out of
126	 * this epic's scope) — matching the same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle the
127	 * `message` prop above already establishes.
128	 *
129	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.6, accessibility sweep): `ZimmInlineMessage` is now programmatically
130	 * associated with the stepper it describes. `messageId` (`useId()`, called unconditionally per
131	 * the rules of hooks) is only ever passed down — as `id` on the rendered `ZimmInlineMessage` and
132	 * as `ariaDescribedBy` on `ZimmQuantityStepper` — when `message` is actually present; with no
133	 * active message there is nothing to describe, so neither prop is passed and both render exactly
134	 * as before this change. `ZimmQuantityStepper` forwards the same id to both its buttons (see that
135	 * component's own docblock for why both, not just one). This required a small, additive addition
136	 * to `ZimmButton`'s icon variant, which had no `aria-describedby` passthrough at all before this
137	 * commit — see that file's own docblock.
138	 */

142	import {
143	  Box,
144	  Fade,

152	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
153	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
154	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
155	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
156	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
157	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
158	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
159	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
160	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
161	import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';
162

168	
169	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
170	
171	type SfccProduct = any;
172	
173	type ProductItemProps = {
174	  product: SfccProduct;
175	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
176	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
177	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
178	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
179	  /**
180	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
181	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
182	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
183	   */
184	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
185	  showLoading?: boolean;
186	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
187	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
188	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
189	  isRemoving?: boolean;
190	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
191	  /**
192	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
193	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
194	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
195	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
196	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
197	   */
198	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
199	  /**
200	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
201	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
202	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
203	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
204	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
205	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
206	   *
207	   * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.6): when present, this component generates an id for the rendered
208	   * ZimmInlineMessage and forwards it as ZimmQuantityStepper's ariaDescribedBy, so the stepper's
209	   * two buttons are programmatically associated with the message describing the state they
210	   * control. `discountLabel` below is a separate, unrelated ZimmInlineMessage instance and is
211	   * NOT given this treatment — a discount is a property of the line item, not a quantity/
212	   * availability state the stepper itself is responsible for.
213	   */
214	  message?: {
215	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
216	    text: string;
217	  };
218	  /**
219	   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
220	   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
221	   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
222	   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
223	   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
224	   *
225	   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
226	   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
227	   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
228	   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
229	   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
230	   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
231	   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
232	   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
233	   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
234	   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
235	   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
236	   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
237	   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
238	   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
239	   * `warning`).

241	  discountLabel?: string;

244	/**
245	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
246	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
247	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
248	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
249	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
250	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
251	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
252	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
253	 */
254	const ProductItem = ({
255	  product,
256	  primaryAction,
257	  secondaryActions,
258	  deliveryActions,
259	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
260	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
261	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
262	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
263	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
264	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
265	  showLoading = false,
266	  containerStyles = {},
267	  isRemoving = false,
268	  pickupInStore = false,
269	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
270	  message,
271	  discountLabel,
272	}: ProductItemProps) => {
273	  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
274	    product,
275	    false,
276	    false,
277	    pickupInStore,
278	  );
279	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
280	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
281	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
282	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
283	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
284	  // SFCC-795 (plan step 3.6): stable per-mount id for the message describing this line's stepper —
285	  // called unconditionally (rules of hooks) but only ever passed down when `message` is actually
286	  // present, see this component's own docblock and the `message` prop's own JSDoc.
287	  const messageId = useId();
288	  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
289	  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
290	  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
291	  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
292	    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
293	      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
294	    );
295	  };
296	  return (
297	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
298	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
299	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
300	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
301	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
302	            <CartItemVariantImage />
303	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
304	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
305	                <Box sx={styles.itemInfoContainer}>
306	                  <Flex sx={styles.itemInfo}>
307	                    <CartItemVariantName />
308	                    <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
309	                  </Flex>
310	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
311	                </Box>
312	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
313	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
314	                )}
315	              </Flex>
316	
317	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
318	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
319	              )}
320	
321	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
322	                <Stack spacing={1}>
323	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
324	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
325	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
326	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
327	                    ) : (
328	                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
329	                        quantity={quantity}
330	                        min={1}
331	                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
332	                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
333	                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
334	                        ariaDescribedBy={message ? messageId : undefined}
335	                      />
336	                    ))}
337	                </Stack>
338	                <Stack>{!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}</Stack>
339	              </Flex>
340	
341	              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
342	                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
343	                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
344	              {discountLabel && (
345	                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
346	              )}
347	
348	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
349	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
350	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock.
351	                  `id={messageId}` (SFCC-795 plan step 3.6) is the other half of the stepper's
352	                  `ariaDescribedBy` above — same id, both sides only present together. */}
353	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} id={messageId} />}
354	
355	              <Box>
356	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
357	                  <Fade in={true}>
358	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
359	                      {inventoryMessage}
360	                    </Text>
361	                  </Fade>
362	                )}
363	              </Box>
364	
365	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
366	            </Stack>
367	          </Flex>
368	
369	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
370	            <HideOnDesktop>
371	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
372	            </HideOnDesktop>
373	          )}
374	        </Stack>
375	      </ItemVariantProvider>
376	    </Box>
377	  );
378	};
379	
380	export default ProductItem;

/*

 * For full license text, see the LICENSE file in the repo root or https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause
 */

/*
 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path
 * rewrites documented below, and a temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live
 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
 *
 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
 * component from a new component":
 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
 *
 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
 *
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
 * tested requirement.
 *
 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
 *
 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): `discountLabel` (optional, prop-driven) renders directly beneath the
 * stepper/price row: DOM order is stepper -> discountLabel -> message -> secondaryActions.
 * "Beneath the stepper" is sourced (session-notes.md line 394's own ticket-summary prose, and the
 * plan's own step 3.3 pass criterion 2 wording); placing it AHEAD of `message` specifically is
 * this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement — no citation
 * in session-notes.md sequences discountLabel relative to message (checked directly, not assumed),
 * and the pass criterion itself is satisfied by "beneath the stepper" alone regardless of order.
 * Chosen because a discount is a property of the line item's own state (always true or false for
 * that line), while `message` is closer to point-of-action feedback nearer the actions row — a
 * reasonable read, not a tested one. Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order.
 * Purely presentational, per session-notes.md §4's SFCC-795 decisions
 * ("Only the discount label is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired
 * when the promotions engine lands"): this component does not compute a discount percentage or
 * label itself; a caller supplies the already-resolved string once something upstream (the
 * promotions engine, and whatever cart-item mapper eventually feeds this component real basket
 * data) is wired — neither is built yet as of this commit. Undefined (every existing caller today)
 * renders nothing — no empty node is emitted. See the prop's own JSDoc below for the styling —
 * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node): a real Figma
 * citation exists now (this paragraph used to say none did, true only in the sense that none had
 * been pulled yet), and the label renders via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"` rather than
 * the bespoke, wrongly-precedented `<Text>` this component used to render directly.
 *
 * The was/now promotional-price mechanism itself (`ListPrice` struck "Was" beside the current
 * "Now", both quantity-scaled) is NOT new at this step and is not touched here — it already lives
 * in base `display-price` (rendered via item-variant/item-price.tsx, unmodified by this commit).
 * See this component's own test file for a disclosed, verified limitation on exactly where that
 * mechanism is and isn't reachable today.
 *
 * SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5, inserted 2026-09-18): the quantity-stepper branch below (the
 * `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity`'s own branch is untouched)
 * now renders `ZimmQuantityStepper` (built and tested at step 3.1) instead of base-styled
 * `ProductQuantityPicker`, with `max` sourced from `getMaxOrderQuantity` (built and tested at
 * step 3.4) and `min={1}` — this component's own tested floor since step 3.1, superseding the old
 * picker's floor of 0, which was never actually speced or tested against any AC.
 * `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component with a different callback contract
 * (`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`, receiving the already-computed next
 * value directly) than the old picker's `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split (which parsed
 * a raw input-change event) — `handleStepperQuantityChange` below is the adapter between the two,
 * and it preserves the old `handleQuantityChange`'s real-mutation-then-conditionally-update-
 * local-state flow exactly: call `onItemQuantityChange` first, only commit the new quantity to
 * local state via `setQuantity` if that call resolves truthy. Writing straight to `setQuantity`
 * instead (skipping the real mutation) would make the stepper look like it works while the real
 * basket on the server silently stops updating. `product-quantity-picker.tsx` itself is untouched
 * and, as of this commit, no longer imported anywhere in this file — left in place per this
 * step's own instruction not to delete a file unasked. `isUnavailable` is left unset on the new
 * stepper — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already out of
 * this epic's scope) — matching the same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle the
 * `message` prop above already establishes.
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.6, accessibility sweep): `ZimmInlineMessage` is now programmatically
 * associated with the stepper it describes. `messageId` (`useId()`, called unconditionally per
 * the rules of hooks) is only ever passed down — as `id` on the rendered `ZimmInlineMessage` and
 * as `ariaDescribedBy` on `ZimmQuantityStepper` — when `message` is actually present; with no
 * active message there is nothing to describe, so neither prop is passed and both render exactly
 * as before this change. `ZimmQuantityStepper` forwards the same id to both its buttons (see that
 * component's own docblock for why both, not just one). This required a small, additive addition
 * to `ZimmButton`'s icon variant, which had no `aria-describedby` passthrough at all before this
 * commit — see that file's own docblock.
 */
import React, { useId } from 'react';

// Chakra Components
import {
  Box,
  Fade,
  Flex,
  Stack,
  Text,
  useMultiStyleConfig,
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

// Project Components
import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
import { ZimmQuantityStepper } from 'app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmQuantityStepper';

// Hooks
import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';

// Utils
import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';

const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';

type SfccProduct = any;

type ProductItemProps = {
  product: SfccProduct;
  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
  /**
   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
   */
  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
  showLoading?: boolean;
  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
  isRemoving?: boolean;
  pickupInStore?: boolean;
  /**
   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
   */
  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
  /**
   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
   *
   * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.6): when present, this component generates an id for the rendered
   * ZimmInlineMessage and forwards it as ZimmQuantityStepper's ariaDescribedBy, so the stepper's
   * two buttons are programmatically associated with the message describing the state they
   * control. `discountLabel` below is a separate, unrelated ZimmInlineMessage instance and is
   * NOT given this treatment — a discount is a property of the line item, not a quantity/
   * availability state the stepper itself is responsible for.
   */
  message?: {
    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
    text: string;
  };
  /**
   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
   *
   * Styling: rendered via `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, not a bespoke element —
   * corrected 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for this exact node, superseding
   * the prior, wrong precedent this JSDoc used to cite). The pulled node is `color:
   * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
   * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption",
   * byte-identical to this codebase's own `status.success` token (green[500] = '#2d5a3d',
   * theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80, registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success) in
   * zimmTokens.ts:73) and the exact same node family `ZimmInlineMessage`'s `error`/`warning`
   * variants already render (regular weight, 12px/18px — see that component's own docblock). The
   * previous version of this comment cited item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part as "the
   * nearest existing sibling treatment" and stated no Figma node existed for this element — both
   * wrong: `colourSize` is a DIFFERENT, MEDIUM-weight node ("Default/Caption-strong", the "Lilac
   * Sand, One size" line), and a real node did exist, just not yet pulled. Confirmed directly
   * with Marcel: no icon on this variant (matching `error`'s own no-icon behaviour, unlike
   * `warning`).
   */
  discountLabel?: string;
};

/**
 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
 */
const ProductItem = ({
  product,
  primaryAction,
  secondaryActions,
  deliveryActions,
  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
  showLoading = false,
  containerStyles = {},
  isRemoving = false,
  pickupInStore = false,
  hideStepperAndActions = false,
  message,
  discountLabel,
}: ProductItemProps) => {
  const { showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
    product,
    false,
    false,
    pickupInStore,
  );
  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
  // SFCC-795 (plan step 3.6): stable per-mount id for the message describing this line's stepper —
  // called unconditionally (rules of hooks) but only ever passed down when `message` is actually
  // present, see this component's own docblock and the `message` prop's own JSDoc.
  const messageId = useId();
  // SFCC-271-250 (plan step 3.5): shared by both ZimmQuantityStepper callbacks below — see this
  // file's own docblock for why this exact call order (real mutation first, conditional local
  // commit second) is load-bearing, not incidental.
  const handleStepperQuantityChange = (nextQuantity: number) => {
    void Promise.resolve(onItemQuantityChange(nextQuantity)).then(
      (isValidChange: boolean) => isValidChange && setQuantity(nextQuantity),
    );
  };
  return (
    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
            <CartItemVariantImage />
            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
                <Box sx={styles.itemInfoContainer}>
                  <Flex sx={styles.itemInfo}>
                    <CartItemVariantName />
                    <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
                  </Flex>
                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
                </Box>
                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
                )}
              </Flex>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
              )}

              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
                    ) : (
                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
                        quantity={quantity}
                        min={1}
                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        ariaDescribedBy={message ? messageId : undefined}
                      />
                    ))}
                </Stack>
                <Stack>{!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}</Stack>
              </Flex>

              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
              {discountLabel && (
                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
              )}

              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock.
                  `id={messageId}` (SFCC-795 plan step 3.6) is the other half of the stepper's
                  `ariaDescribedBy` above — same id, both sides only present together. */}
              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} id={messageId} />}

              <Box>
                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
                  <Fade in={true}>
                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
                      {inventoryMessage}
                    </Text>
                  </Fade>
                )}
              </Box>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
            </Stack>
          </Flex>

          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
            <HideOnDesktop>
              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
            </HideOnDesktop>
          )}
        </Stack>
      </ItemVariantProvider>
    </Box>
  );
};

export default ProductItem;

1	/**
2	 * Commerce/ProductItem — Storybook stories for the cart line-item shell (SFCC-270, plan
3	 * step 2.2), restyled to the Figma cart-item spec.
4	 *
5	 * Providers supplied by .storybook/preview.tsx: IntlProvider, ChakraProvider.
6	 * This file adds its own inert provider stack, matching product-view/index.stories.tsx's own
7	 * documented pattern (see that file for the full rationale):
8	 *   MemoryRouter — item-name.tsx's <Link> (react-router-dom) and useMultiSite (via
9	 *     MultiSiteProvider below) both need Router/site context.
10	 *   MultiSiteProvider — useMultiSite (item-name.tsx's <Link>'s buildUrl, and
11	 *     StoreLocatorProvider below, which reads the current site to namespace its localStorage key).
12	 *   StoreLocatorProvider — `useDerivedProduct` (via item-price.tsx/item-attributes.tsx's own
13	 *     transitive dependency chain) unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`
14	 *     (`use-selected-store.js`), which throws `'useSelectedStore must be used within a
15	 *     StoreLocatorProvider'` with no Provider present — round 2 rework fix, confirmed by reading
16	 *     that hook's source, not assumed. Nested inside MultiSiteProvider (its own body calls
17	 *     useMultiSite()), outside CommerceProviders (its one consumer, `useSelectedStore`'s internal
18	 *     `useStores` call, resolves with `enabled: false` here since no story sets a selected store
19	 *     in localStorage, so it never actually needs Commerce context — but this file nests it
20	 *     inside CommerceProviders anyway for a single consistent provider order). `config={{}}` is a
21	 *     deliberately empty stand-in — no story here drives real store-locator state, so there is no
22	 *     real config value to supply; PropTypes will warn on the missing required fields, which is
23	 *     inert noise, not a render failure.
24	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — item-attributes.tsx's usePromotions/
25	 *     useProducts/useProduct/useCurrentBasket (via
26	 *     `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-basket`). `disableAuthInit` +
27	 *     an `.invalid` proxy URL prevent any real network calls; none of this story's mock line
28	 *     items carry priceAdjustments/bundledProductItems/type.bundle, so every one of those
29	 *     hooks resolves with `enabled: false` and never actually fetches.
30	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (item-price.tsx, product-item/index.tsx itself).
31	 *   ServerContext.Provider (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`, not commerce-sdk-react) —
32	 *     found live in Storybook, not anticipated: item-attributes.tsx's useCurrentBasket() call
33	 *     above has its own separate transitive chain (useSFPayments -> useAppOrigin -> useOrigin)
34	 *     that calls the SDK's useServerContext() and destructures `res` from it unconditionally.
35	 *     With no Provider, useContext returns undefined and the destructure throws before useOrigin's
36	 *     own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res` at all) is reached.
37	 *     `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
38	 *     client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.

10	 *
11	 * @param {Object} imageGroups - The product/variations image groups you want to search.
12	 * @param {Object} options - Search criteria to match on the ImageGroup object.
13	 * @param {string} options.viewType - Typically this refers to image sizes like small, medium, large. But can vary based on your back-end configuration.
14	 * @param {Object} options.selectedVariationAttributes - A key/value object consisting of attibute id's and their values.
15	 * @returns {Object} - The ImageGroup matching the search criteria
16	 */
17	export const findImageGroupBy = (imageGroups = [], options) => {
18	    let {viewType, selectedVariationAttributes = {}} = options
19	
20	    // Start by filtering out any imageGroup that isn't the correct viewType.
21	    imageGroups = imageGroups.filter(
22	        ({viewType: imageGroupViewType}) => imageGroupViewType === viewType
23	    )
24	
25	    // Not all variation attributes are reflected in images. For example, you probably
26	    // won't have a separate image group for various sizes, but you might for colors. For that
27	    // reason we need to know what are valid attribute values to filter on.
28	    const refinableAttributeIds = [
29	        ...new Set(
30	            imageGroups
31	                .reduce((acc, {variationAttributes = []}) => [...acc, ...variationAttributes], [])
32	                .map(({id}) => id)
33	        )
34	    ]
35	
36	    // Update the `selectedVariationAttributes` by filtering out the attributes that have no
37	    // representation in this imageGroup.
38	    selectedVariationAttributes = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes).reduce((acc, curr) => {
39	        return refinableAttributeIds.includes(curr)
40	            ? {
41	                  ...acc,
42	                  [`${curr}`]: selectedVariationAttributes[curr]
43	              }
44	            : acc
45	    }, {})
46	
47	    // Find the image group that has all the all the selected variation value attributes.
48	    imageGroups = imageGroups.find(({variationAttributes = []}) => {
49	        const selectedIds = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes)
50	
51	        return selectedIds.every((selectedId) => {
52	            const selectedValue = selectedVariationAttributes[selectedId]
53	
54	            return variationAttributes.find(
55	                ({id, values}) =>
56	                    id === selectedId && values.every(({value}) => value === selectedValue)
57	            )
58	        })
59	    })
60	
61	    return imageGroups
62	}
63
